title: Pediatric Infusion Concentrations
sources: Standardize 4 Safety (S4S) pediatric continuous-infusion standard concentrations

changelog.change: Initial entry — standard-concentration vs rule-of-6 approaches, a common-infusion table with usual dose ranges, and the conversion the peds-drip-rate calculator uses.

purpose: Pick an infusion concentration and know the usual dose range. Enter the chosen concentration and the target dose into the Weight-Based Infusion Rate calculator to get mL/hr.

items: Standard concentration (preferred, safest): every patient gets the same bag concentration for a given drug; the pump rate varies. Fewer compounding errors, supports smart-pump limits. Use the S4S concentrations.

Rule of 6 (legacy, for improvised situations): to get 1 mL/hr = 0.1 mcg/kg/min, put (0.6 × weight in kg) mg of drug into a total of 100 mL. For 1 mL/hr = 1 mcg/kg/min, use (6 × weight) mg in 100 mL. Requires an individualised bag per patient — error-prone; avoid where standard concentrations exist.

body.text: Rate (mL/hr) = dose (mcg/kg/min) × weight (kg) × 60 ÷ concentration (mcg/mL). For a dose in mcg/kg/hr, drop the × 60. The Weight-Based Infusion Rate calculator does this — pick a concentration above, enter the target dose and weight.

Concentrations vary by institution and by fluid-restriction needs (a neonate or a cardiac patient may need a 2–4× concentrated bag). Always confirm against your unit's standard-concentration list and the smart-pump library. Prostaglandin E1 causes apnoea — have airway support ready when starting it.

buildNote: Companion to the peds-drip-rate formula calculator. Standard concentrations per Standardize 4 Safety; ranges are usual starting/PICU ranges, not caps.
